Q: Next.js, why? Warning: Prop `style` did not match. Server: "object-fit: cover;" Client: "object-fit:cover" A:

run :

npm add --dev babel-plugin-styled-components

then create a .babelrc in your src folder and add :

{
    "presets": ["next/babel"],
    "plugins": [["styled-components", { "ssr": true }]]
}

Q: Database driver error when loading data with Informatica into Oracle XE 10 g A:

From the error message, it appears that you have installed 32-bit Oracle client and 64-bit PowerCenter.

A 64 bit PowerCenter works only with 64 bit oracle client. Please install 64-bit Oracle client, restart PowerCenter services and check if the session succeeds.

Few comments about the discussion in this thread:

  • Make sure %oracle_home%/bin is added as a first entry in the PATH variable. Informatica recommends so.
  • After you change PATH variable, Informatica services needs to be restarted for that to take effect.
  • pmora8.dll will be available in %INFA_HOME%/server/bin
  • PM_HOME is for PowerCenter 7.x or earlier versions. From 8.x it is INFA_HOME

Q: Why does tkinter not accept self=None in this case? A:

Problem is because you use CTkLabel in wrong way.

You have to create instance of class using () and later use place() without self.
You have also text and bg in wrong place.

CTkLabel(app, text="{guess[i]}", bg_color="green").place(x=120+(i*30),y=guessCount*25)

or keeping it in variable (to have access to label later)

my_label = CTkLabel(app, text="{guess[i]}", bg_color="green")
my_label.place(x=120+(i*30), y=guessCount*25)

Official documentation for CTkLabel shows similar example (but without place/pack/grid)

label = customtkinter.CTkLabel(app, text="CTkLabel", fg_color="transparent")

Minimal working code

import customtkinter as ctk

app = ctk.CTk()

my_label = ctk.CTkLabel(app, text="Hello World!", bg_color="green")
my_label.place(x=10, y=10)

app.mainloop()

Q: What is the intended use-case for git stash? A:

You can use the following commands:

  • To save your uncommitted changes

    git stash

  • To list your saved stashes

    git stash list

  • To apply/get back the uncommitted changes where x is 0,1,2...

    git stash apply stash@{x}

Note:

  • To apply a stash and remove it from the stash list

    git stash pop stash@{x}

  • To apply a stash and keep it in the stash list

    git stash apply stash@{x}

Q: C++ convert vector element to string A:

Also read Why can't the std::string constructor take just a char? for a good reason why you can't do this.

Pay special attention to the use of curly braces in list.push_back(std::string{ example[index] });. This is using list initialization.

With the regular std::string constructors the best you could do is list.push_back( std::string( 1, example[index] )); (make a string holding example[index] repeated 1 time). Also note that because std::string has a list initializer, you have to be a bit careful with what is sometimes called "uniform initialization" as list.push_back(std::string{ 1, example[index] }); still parses as a list, assuming the 1 means the character with the encoded value of 1 and provides a string that is 2 characters long, not 1, and that first character is probably non-printable.
